// MIT. Public, descriptor-driven StellarExpert workspace contract.
export const SOURCE_CONTRACT = Object.freeze({
  provider: 'StellarExpert Open API', version: '1.4.0',
  baseUrl: 'https://api.stellar.expert',
  documentation: 'https://github.com/stellar-expert/stellar-expert-explorer/blob/308ef220358192911525272d9ad251225dd1e00b/open-api/openapi.yml',
  repository: 'https://github.com/stellar-expert/stellar-expert-explorer',
  sourceCommit: '308ef220358192911525272d9ad251225dd1e00b',
  openapiBlob: 'f83ee631d9e50a0b7eeb3d7d3ed5db28f92fb1b4',
  terms: 'https://stellar.expert/',
  ratingMeaning: 'Ledger activity popularity indicators, as described by StellarExpert.',
  observationMeaning: 'A retained sequence of provider responses observed over the recorded time interval. The provider does not advertise snapshot isolation across pages.',
  amountMeaning: 'Original numeric tokens are strings. Holder balance and documented traded/payment amounts are stroops; the supply endpoint returns decimal asset units. The AssetInfo supply field is retained without an undocumented unit conversion.'
});
export const CAPTURE_KINDS = [
  {id:'assets',label:'Asset search',paginated:true,fields:['network','search','sort','order','limit']},
  {id:'holders',label:'Asset holders',paginated:true,fields:['network','asset','limit']},
  {id:'rating',label:'Asset activity rating',paginated:false,fields:['network','asset']},
  {id:'supply',label:'Issued supply',paginated:false,fields:['network','asset']},
  {id:'directory',label:'Account directory',paginated:true,fields:['address','tag','search','order','limit']},
  {id:'tags',label:'Directory tag definitions',paginated:false,fields:[]},
  {id:'blocked-domains',label:'Community-reported domains',paginated:true,fields:['search','order','limit']},
  {id:'domain',label:'Domain listing lookup',paginated:false,fields:['domain']},
  {id:'ledger-time',label:'Ledger at or before timestamp',paginated:false,fields:['network','timestamp']},
  {id:'ledger-sequence',label:'Ledger closing time',paginated:false,fields:['network','sequence']}
];
export const COLUMNS = Object.freeze({
  assets:['asset','domain','created','supply','traded_amount','traded_units','payments_amount','payment_units','trustlines_total','trustlines_authorized','trustlines_funded','trades','payments','rating_average','rating_age','rating_trades','rating_payments','rating_trustlines','rating_volume7d','rating_interop','rating_liquidity','toml_json','paging_token'],
  holders:['asset','account','balance_stroops','balance_units','paging_token'],
  rating:['asset','rating_average','rating_age','rating_trades','rating_payments','rating_trustlines','rating_volume7d','rating_interop','rating_liquidity','rating_json'],
  supply:['asset','supply_units'],
  directory:['address','name','domain','tags_json','paging_token'],
  tags:['name','description'],
  'blocked-domains':['domain','paging_token'],
  domain:['domain','blocked'],
  'ledger-time':['sequence','timestamp','date'],
  'ledger-sequence':['sequence','timestamp','date']
});
export const SOURCE_COLUMNS = ['sourcePageSha256','sourceRecord','sourceObservedAt','sourceUrl'];
export const ACTIONS = {
  'watch.add':['network','asset','label','note'], 'watch.remove':['watchId'],
  'capture.start':['query','label','watchId','pageBudget'], 'capture.resume':['captureId','pageBudget'],
  'edition.select':['editionId'], 'edition.compare':['leftId','rightId'],
  'annotation.save':['editionId','subject','note','status'],
  'dataset.prepare':['editionId','name'], 'dataset.query':['datasetId','query'],
  'release.prepare':['datasetId','origin','path','payment'], 'release.inspect':['releaseId'],
  'release.activate':['releaseId','expectedGeneration'],'release.start':['releaseId','expectedGeneration'],
  'release.stop':['releaseId'],'release.rollback':['releaseId','expectedGeneration'],
  'buyer.inspect':['intentIds'], 'buyer.receive':['intentIds'],
  'export.create':['editionId','format']
};
export function workspaceSchema({inboxConfigured=false}={}) {
  return {
    schema:'stellar-forge.stellar-expert-workspace-schema.v1', source:SOURCE_CONTRACT,
    networks:['public','testnet'], captureKinds:CAPTURE_KINDS,
    fields:{
      network:{type:'select',options:['public','testnet'],default:'public'},
      asset:{type:'text',label:'XLM or CODE-GISSUER (optional -1/-2 type suffix)'},
      search:{type:'text'}, address:{type:'array',maxItems:50},tag:{type:'array',maxItems:10},
      sort:{type:'select',options:['rating','created','payments','trades','trustlines','volume','volume7d'],default:'rating'},
      order:{type:'select',options:['asc','desc'],default:'desc'},
      limit:{type:'integer',minimum:1,maximum:200,default:100},
      domain:{type:'text'},timestamp:{type:'text'},sequence:{type:'text',pattern:'^[1-9][0-9]*$'}
    },
    datasetTables:COLUMNS, sourceColumns:SOURCE_COLUMNS,
    paymentFields:['scheme','network','asset','amount','payTo','maxTimeoutSeconds'],
    paymentSchema:{scheme:{type:'select',options:['exact'],default:'exact'},network:{type:'select',options:['stellar:testnet','stellar:pubnet'],default:'stellar:testnet'},
      asset:{type:'text',label:'Explicit SEP-41 token contract'},payTo:{type:'text',label:'Explicit merchant receiving address'},
      amount:{type:'text',label:'Positive atomic units',pattern:'^[1-9][0-9]*$',maximum:'170141183460469231731687303715884105727'},
      maxTimeoutSeconds:{type:'integer',minimum:1,maximum:86400,default:300}},
    actions:ACTIONS, annotationStatuses:['open','reviewed','follow_up'],
    exportFormats:['json','csv','report'], inboxConfigured,
    limits:{pageBudget:1000,pageBytes:8*1024*1024,captureBytes:128*1024*1024,records:250000,rowsPerView:500},
    bootstrap:{fragment:'bearer token',header:'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN',storage:'sessionStorage'},
    revisionPolicy:'Operation identity is reconciled before expectedRevision. New mutations require the current workspace revision.'
  };
}

# Shared supplier accounts

A merchant can use one supplier account behind several paid routes or seller
processes. This module gives those original dispatches one shared call allowance
and keeps the supplier's rate-limit cooldown with the account.

The integration composes the maintained Routescan quota engine. Its existing
atomic reservation, process lock, saved state and recovery behavior remain the
account owner. The original SF30 upstream dispatcher checks that account before
contacting the supplier.

## Configure the existing upstream seller

Add a **supplierAccounts** object to the existing
**stellar-forge.seller-upstreams.v1** configuration. Keep its existing routes,
request mappings, secrets references, cache and delivery settings.

The following is the supplier-account portion to compose into that file:

~~~json
{
  "supplierAccounts": {
    "market-data": {
      "directory": "/var/lib/starforge/suppliers/market-data",
      "account": "market-data-primary",
      "apiKeyEnv": "DATA_FEED_API_KEY",
      "requestsPerSecond": 3,
      "callsPerDay": 1000
    }
  }
}
~~~

Set **supplierAccount** to **"market-data"** on each existing upstream binding
that uses this allowance. A binding keeps its original authentication and request
mapping; the new field selects the shared quota account.

| Field | Operator meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Account alias | The key in **supplierAccounts**; bindings select this alias. |
| **directory** | An absolute private directory shared by seller processes using this account. |
| **account** | The stable label used by the original quota ledger. Keep it with the existing account. |
| **apiKeyEnv** | Optional environment-variable reference used for the quota account's identity. |
| **requestsPerSecond** | Shared original-dispatch rate, from 1 to 1,000 calls per second. |
| **callsPerDay** | Shared rolling 24-hour allowance, from 1 to 100,000,000 calls. |
| Binding **supplierAccount** | The configured alias used for this route's original supplier dispatches. |

Use the same directory, account identity and policy for processes drawing from
the same allowance. Keep the original private directory when restarting or
moving the service into its maintained runtime. Separate supplier accounts use
separate state directories.

The allowance unit is an original supplier call. Configure it from the
supplier's account limits. Provider tariffs expressed as credits, weighted
operations or currency continue through their existing provider-specific tariff
calculation.

## Operate the account

Start the original upstream seller with its existing upstream configuration and
operations listener. Open the listener's seller operations page, then choose
**Supplier accounts**.

1. Select **Load supplier accounts**. The listener reads each account's original
   local state and shows the capture time.
2. Review the shared account table. It includes original route membership,
   rolling-window calls, remaining calls, per-second allowance, admission and
   retry time.
3. Select **View** beside an account to inspect its policy, state revision,
   dispatch reservations, last dispatch, provider cooldown and route bindings.
4. Select **Refresh snapshot** after traffic or a recovery operation to read
   current state.
5. Download **Snapshot JSON** or **Account CSV** to hand over the exact displayed
   snapshot. Filtering the table leaves the complete account set in these
   downloads.

The page uses explicit refreshes. A failed refresh keeps the previous snapshot
and its timestamp visible. Individual unavailable accounts remain visible while
other configured accounts can still be reviewed. The account's safe error code
appears in its detail panel.

The installed Starforge release provides the same operator command:

~~~sh
starforge supplier-quotas check --upstreams /private/seller-upstreams.json
starforge supplier-quotas inspect --upstreams /private/seller-upstreams.json --account market-data
~~~

Application code can import **createSupplierQuotaRegistry** and
**attachSupplierQuota** from
**@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/seller/supplier-quotas**, and
**compileSupplierAccounts** from its **/config** export. The same named functions
are also available from the package root.

The source checkout provides the corresponding local operator command:

~~~sh
node sf30-seller-sdk/supplier-quota/cli.mjs check --upstreams /private/seller-upstreams.json
node sf30-seller-sdk/supplier-quota/cli.mjs inspect --upstreams /private/seller-upstreams.json
node sf30-seller-sdk/supplier-quota/cli.mjs inspect --upstreams /private/seller-upstreams.json --account market-data
~~~

**check** validates the existing configuration without opening its quota state.
**inspect** reads the original account state and prints the shared snapshot;
it exits with status 2 when a selected account is unavailable.

## Admission and retained state

The original quota engine accounts conservatively for a rolling 24 hours using
one-minute buckets. Every original supplier dispatch reserves one call
atomically. A request that has entered that dispatch path keeps its reservation
when the supplier or network later fails.

The reservation runs at the original dispatch boundary after the existing
request preparation, credentials, cache and idempotency behavior. Cached
responses and completed request replays keep their original path. A real cache
miss or new mutation checks the shared account before its supplier call.

An original supplier HTTP 429 response records its Retry-After cooldown on this
same account. Other bindings and processes see that cooldown through the
existing persisted quota state. Restarting the seller reopens the original
account.

| Display state | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| Accepting calls | The saved snapshot allowed another original supplier dispatch; dispatch checks current state again. |
| Supplier cooldown | The supplier's original cooldown extends beyond the snapshot time. |
| Window limit | The account's rolling-window call allowance is used. |
| Rate limit | The configured shared call rate requires a delay. |
| Unavailable | The account's original state could not be read; inspect its configuration and retained directory. |

**retryAt** is an absolute UTC time from the original quota engine.
**retryAfterSeconds** is the corresponding delay when that snapshot was taken.
A displayed past retry time means it is time to refresh the view.

Configuration checking and unpaid challenge handling keep their existing
state-free path. The original quota state opens lazily for an explicit account
snapshot, admission or supplier dispatch.

## Operator API and exports

The existing private operations listener serves these routes:

| Route | Response |
| --- | --- |
| **GET /supplier-quotas** | Supplier-account operator screen. |
| **GET /api/supplier-quotas** | Current account snapshot. |
| **GET /supplier-quotas.json** | Current account snapshot as a JSON download. |
| **GET /supplier-quotas.csv** | Current account snapshot as a CSV download. |

These reads retain the listener's host, origin, method and cache controls. Each
API or export request reads current local account state. Browser download
buttons instead export the exact already displayed snapshot.

The JSON schema is **stellar-forge.supplier-quotas.v1**. It contains **enabled**,
**capturedAt** and an **accounts** array. Each account has its alias, original
binding names, availability, safe error code and projected original quota fields.
Quota fields include the stable account label, policy, rolling-window totals,
dispatch timestamps, cooldown, retry time and saved revision. Credential values
and private state paths remain in the existing service configuration.

CSV contains one row per account and retains the same capture time. Labels are
quoted and spreadsheet-formula prefixes are protected. Unavailable accounts
retain their aliases, bindings and safe error codes; their unavailable numeric
fields are empty.

A seller without the shared supplier service returns **enabled: false** and an
empty account list, and the screen presents the configuration step. An account
read failure affects that account's row. A failure to obtain the complete service
snapshot returns **503 SUPPLIER_QUOTA_UNAVAILABLE**.

## Continue the original installation

Keep this module with the same SF30 seller SDK, original Routescan quota engine
and operations assets in the maintained Starforge release. Continue the
existing merchant's upstream file and account directories when receiving or
upgrading that release.

The shared account service supports the same original provider adapters. Start
adoption with one real account and its actual provider limits; attach the
additional bindings that draw from that account, then review one account
snapshot from the original running merchant.

# Federal awards and workshares in Applications

Open **Federal awards and workshares** from the installed Merchant Workspace Applications page. This is the original USAspending browser and saved award workspace, including transaction history, prime workshare assessments, complete source exports and customer receiving.

## Save a research application

Select the installed runtime containing the USAspending contribution and choose **Federal awards and workshares**.

Choose a private research workspace. An existing workspace reopens its original awards.sqlite3 database, award editions, exact source pages, modifications, saved reviews and receiving records. For a new workspace, choose a new folder beneath a private parent; saving the application creates the selected folder, and its first launch initializes the original award workspace.

Optionally select a private **Customer delivery folder**. The browser can receive original customer delivery directories from that folder through its existing receiving operation. A new selected folder is created when the application is saved. Use the **Operator name** for attribution on workspace operations and saved assessments. A local port of 0 selects an available loopback port.

Review and save the application, then review and start its original operation. **Open** uses the private browser link announced by that running workspace. Keep the link on the host where the application runs; it contains the browser session token.

The saved application retains its chosen workspace, operator, receiving folder and runtime. The original Applications lifecycle retains the run, process state, output and stop operation.

## Work through an award

The award browser keeps the complete research workflow:

1. Save the actual federal-award search and capture all original provider pages.
2. Open an award edition, retain the original award detail, and prepare a prime workshare against that source.
3. Open transaction history for the selected award. Capture or receive its actual transaction pages, inspect modification numbers, agency action descriptions, exact funding changes and fiscal-year totals, and compare retained captures.
4. Save the complete workshare assessment with its fit, proposed delivery, deliverables, acceptance and next action.
5. Export the original transaction capture, CSV or combined workshare brief. Choose private-review inclusion explicitly when preparing an assessment handover.
6. Receive the original award edition before its transactions. The transaction receiver keeps the selected source, saved review lineage and replay identity.
7. Use the existing whole-workspace backup and restore to carry the saved research and original transaction source into another workspace.

The transaction workflow and original provider contract are described in [TRANSACTIONS.md](TRANSACTIONS.md). The award source and dossier workflow remain documented in [README.md](README.md) and [DOSSIER.md](DOSSIER.md).

## Stop and reopen saved work

Use **Stop** on the original Applications run. The original USAspending server pauses active provider operations, waits for their retained state and closes the same workspace database. The application remains saved.

Start that application again to reopen the same research directory. It receives a new private session link and preserves the existing award editions, captured transaction pages, saved assessments, original operation history and customer receiving. Resume an interrupted source capture by its existing capture identity; the workspace retains its original request, accepted pages and continuation.

The launcher checks the selected workspace identity, original application source and running session before retaining the browser link. If a selected directory or installed source has changed, review the current selection in Applications. The small authenticated session endpoint identifies the original running process without transferring the complete research inventory.

## Original command

The installed command is:

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-application serve \
  --workspace /PRIVATE_PARENT/award-research \
  --operator "Research desk" \
  --receiving-root /PRIVATE_PARENT/customer-deliveries \
  --port 0
~~~

From a complete source checkout, invoke the same command with Node 22.13 or newer:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/usaspending/application.mjs serve \
  --workspace /PRIVATE_PARENT/award-research \
  --port 0
~~~

The command prints one structured startup line containing the private browser URL and the original workspace session identity. SIGINT or SIGTERM invokes the original server close operation. The existing usaspending-research and usaspending-dossier commands operate the same saved product.

## Source-owned installation

The usaspending distribution contribution declares the application, original research and dossier commands, and ./research/usaspending/application export. Its provider consumes the maintained Applications preparation, retained operation, startup observer and stop/reopen lifecycle.

The application source selection includes the existing award, transaction and browser modules plus its source-specific startup adapter. The installed runtime and managed release remain the original source owners. The launcher verifies the selected source in both locations and authenticates the original /api/identity before the shared observer saves the launch link.

## Continue the original native receiving operation

The maintained receiver consumes the completed transaction receiving directory.
It reopens the original SQLite workspace and source capture, retains the browser
announcement through the original Applications provider, stops the original
process, and reopens its saved transactions and assessment. It also opens a new
workspace, restores the original complete workspace, and reopens that restored
research.

From the complete original source materialized under DELIVERY/source:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/usaspending/application-native.mjs \
  --received /PRIVATE_DELIVERY/native \
  --out /PRIVATE_DELIVERY/applications-source
```

For the full installed Applications lifecycle, supply the actual READY runtime
containing this contribution:

```sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/usaspending/application-native.mjs \
  --received /PRIVATE_DELIVERY/native \
  --runtime /PRIVATE_RUNTIME/federal-awards \
  --out /PRIVATE_DELIVERY/applications-managed
```

The managed run calls the existing workspace model to attach the retained runtime,
review and save both an existing and a new application, adopt its original release,
launch its original worker, retain its private browser URL, stop the operation,
and reopen the application after closing the operator workspace. The new-folder
case passes through the existing save-time directory creation and fresh start
preparation. It then restores the original transaction workspace into the new
folder and reopens that saved application.

The result identifies its actual mode as original-source-application or
original-managed-applications. Each creates application-receiving-result.json,
original operation records, session identities, complete workspace exports,
transaction CSVs, workshare documents, and the saved original assessment.
Use the same original operation ID, SCF-USASPENDING-AWARD-TRANSACTIONS-64B7-20261012,
and the existing receiving output. Both runs use the retained award and source
bytes already delivered with that operation.

# Federal award research in the original SF88 dossier

The USAspending workspace captures award searches, keeps their original pages,
enriches selected awards with original details and saves immutable editions.
This receiving bridge carries that same edition into the maintained research
dossier, where an operator can ask questions, review evidence, write cited
findings and export a complete portable project.

Use the original award workspace or its complete saved edition export. The
bridge makes no provider request and starts no purchase. The original SF30
merchant and SF88 customer remain the acquisition path for a purchased edition.

## Start with a saved edition

The installed command is:

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-dossier help
~~~

The source command, from the repository root, is:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/usaspending/dossier-cli.mjs help
~~~

Use the current Node 22.13+ runtime with built-in SQLite and JSON source-number
context. All file and workspace arguments must be absolute paths. Keep private
workspaces in a private directory whose parent exists.

Create a project using the existing dossier command, then add a question using
the returned project ID and revision:

~~~sh
starforge research-dossiers create \
  --store /private/research-dossiers \
  --title "Federal implementation partnerships" \
  --description "Current prime awards and the implementation work our team can deliver"

starforge research-dossiers question \
  --store /private/research-dossiers \
  --id RETURNED_DOSSIER_ID \
  --revision RETURNED_REVISION \
  --text "Which captured awards fit our technical work, and which source facts support an initial workshare?"
~~~

Retain the returned dossier ID, question ID and current revision. The same
operator can create or edit them in the industrial research workspace.

Receive an existing immutable award edition directly:

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-dossier receive \
  --store /private/research-dossiers \
  --id RETURNED_DOSSIER_ID \
  --question RETURNED_QUESTION_ID \
  --revision CURRENT_REVISION \
  --award-dir /private/award-research \
  --edition ORIGINAL_EDITION_ID
~~~

Or receive the original complete edition export:

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-dossier inspect \
  --file /private/delivery/original-award-edition.json

starforge usaspending-dossier receive \
  --store /private/research-dossiers \
  --id RETURNED_DOSSIER_ID \
  --question RETURNED_QUESTION_ID \
  --revision CURRENT_REVISION \
  --file /private/delivery/original-award-edition.json
~~~

The result includes the source signature, original edition and packet identities,
retained component bindings, coverage and current dossier revision. An optional
--out saves that import result to a new file. An identical packet export or the first completed
receipt for the same import is reused. Different existing output is preserved.

Saved analyst reviews are excluded by default. Use --include-reviews when
explicitly receiving an edition export that includes those private reviews.
The existing export is otherwise kept complete, including any original native
buyer delivery stored in its metadata.

## Use the retained source

Open the existing research operator:

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-dossier open --store /private/research-dossiers
~~~

The command prints its loopback URL and session token. The workspace offers the
existing project, question, evidence and finding controls. For each award,
the complete typed row and original record remain available together. Sources
are grouped by the original USAspending award URL; a later edition preserves a
separate source occurrence and any changed content.

A practical research pass is:

1. Read the captured query dates, filters and coverage before choosing a prime.
2. Inspect the original recipient, parent recipient, agency, award description,
   performance dates and amount fields.
3. Add separately captured company or opportunity sources to the same research
   question using the existing research-result import.
4. Select evidence and write the concrete technical workshare as an analyst
   finding, citing the source records that support the proposed fit.
5. Export the source-backed report and portable project for the relationship
   owner or receiving engineer.

The bridge preserves complete records; selecting evidence controls what the
analyst emphasizes. A source record establishes the reported award facts. The
operator supplies technical fit, implementation scope, deliverables, acceptance
criteria and commercial terms in the finding.

### Read amount and identity fields correctly

| Field | Preserved meaning |
| --- | --- |
| award_amount_usd | Original award-search amount, or the detail record's total obligation. |
| total_obligation_usd | Original detail total_obligation value. |
| exercised_usd | Original base_exercised_options value. |
| potential_usd | Original base_and_all_options value. |
| outlays_usd | Original reported outlay value; null remains unknown. |
| recipient_uei | Identity of the award recipient. |
| parent_recipient_uei | Separate parent-company identity from the original detail. |
| parent_award_key | Separate parent-award identity. |
| source_kind | Original search, original detail, or original buyer delivery. |

All monetary fields remain exact decimal strings. They are never passed through
floating-point formatting or added together across unlike fields. Missing amounts
remain null. Search coverage, enrichment coverage and the current edition's
selection remain separate in the retained coverage object.

Original source references:

- [USAspending API](https://api.usaspending.gov/)
- [API documentation](https://api.usaspending.gov/docs/)
- [Official source and API contracts](https://github.com/fedspendingtransparency/usaspending-api)
- [Original research dossier](../../sf88-operator-buyer-cli/research-dossiers/README.md)

## Exact saved-edition Node integration

Inside an existing original customer operation, pass the already-open
AwardWorkspace and DossierStore. Their existing owners manage their lifetimes:

~~~js
import {receiveUSAspendingEdition} from './dossier.mjs';

const project = await originalDossiers.get(dossierId);
const received = await receiveUSAspendingEdition(originalDossiers, dossierId, {
  workspace: originalAwardWorkspace,
  editionId: originalReceivedEditionId,
  questionId,
  expectedRevision: project.revision,
  includeReviews: false,
});
~~~

The bridge calls:

~~~js
originalAwardWorkspace.exportEdition(originalReceivedEditionId, {
  includeSourceBytes: true,
  includeReviews: false,
});
~~~

exactly once. It checks the packet digest, immutable edition digest, typed row
digests and original page/detail bytes before writing. The same import works on
an already-exported packet by passing packet instead of workspace.

A complete import creates one metadata component and as many size-aware source
components as the existing response limit requires. All rows, original search
pages, detailed responses, original native delivery archives and remaining packet
metadata are retained. Empty
cohorts still retain their original query and coverage. Each component uses the
original dossier store's exclusive immutable revisions and content-addressed
source storage.

The stable source signature excludes only the export timestamp and the packet's
derived digest. A retry with the current dossier revision reuses completed
components and the first export metadata. Source changes produce a new signature
and new edition occurrences. A conflict from another writer returns the ordinary
REVISION_CONFLICT; the original project remains available at its current revision.
A partial receiving failure carries error.usaSpendingImport with the completed
bindings, allowing the caller to resume the same import.

An optional signal cancels between components. onComponent(binding, progress)
receives the actual saved or reused component. Neither option changes the source
edition or its acquisition state.

The import uses the dossier's existing limits: 64 MiB per retained response,
8 MiB per revision and 256 MiB for a portable export. A single oversized source
record is reported before any import write. Use a selected immutable edition for
a research project that exceeds the portable dossier size.

## Preview the original edition through the provider registry

The operator can also read an original award edition through the existing
provider registry:

~~~js
import {startDossierWorkspace} from '../../sf88-operator-buyer-cli/research-dossiers/server.mjs';
import {createUSAspendingEditionProvider} from './dossier.mjs';

const app = await startDossierWorkspace({
  directory: '/private/research-dossiers',
  providers: {
    usaspending: createUSAspendingEditionProvider(originalAwardWorkspace),
  },
});
~~~

The equivalent installed command is:

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-dossier open \
  --store /private/research-dossiers \
  --award-dir /private/award-research
~~~

Attach provider usaspending with reference {"editionId":"ORIGINAL_EDITION_ID"}.
The original award key is the stable source handle. Coverage and warning state
remain visible, and the original workspace owns access and acquisition.

Use receive for a complete portable source copy. Provider attachment uses the
dossier's existing reference mode: notes, findings and original handles persist,
while its provider view is read from the configured original workspace.

## Reports, portable reopening and exact packet recovery

Use the existing export commands:

~~~sh
starforge research-dossiers export \
  --store /private/research-dossiers --id DOSSIER_ID \
  --format html --out /private/delivery/award-research.html

starforge research-dossiers export \

starforge research-dossiers export \
~~~

# USAspending award research operator

A complete local research workspace for federal prime contract awards. Save an agency or service cohort, retain each official request and response, enrich the resulting awards with their original detail records, qualify a prime and a proposed workshare, compare a later edition, and deliver the resulting dataset through the existing Stellar Forge merchant and receiving tools.

The operator includes an industrial browser workspace, a command line, a durable SQLite store, exact decimal values, a portable research packet, and the original SF88 research-dossier integration. Its public dataset projection contains award research; the analyst's contacts, pricing, proposal notes, and disposition remain in the private workspace and explicitly requested review exports.

## Start the workspace

Use Node 24 (Node 22.13+ with node:sqlite and JSON.parse source context is also supported). The research core has no third-party package dependency. Run from the complete Stellar Forge source tree so the existing SF30 dataset, SF100 receiving, and SF88 dossier modules are available.

Installed command:

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-research serve \
  --workspace /private/federal-award-research \
  --operator "Research operator"
~~~

Equivalent source command:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/usaspending/cli.mjs serve \
  --workspace /private/federal-award-research \
  --operator "Research operator"
~~~

Open the complete URL printed by the command. The server listens on 127.0.0.1 and gives that session a private capability in the URL fragment. The browser uses it for authenticated workspace requests. The interface supports:

- Saved cohorts and source capture, including actual source pages, pause/resume, and explicit capacity changes.
- Searchable award editions with current and parent prime identities, original order and parent award identifiers, agency, procurement, amount, and performance fields.
- Detail enrichment and a named selection of actual award IDs.
- An analyst shortlist and full workshare record, including capability source URLs, scope, deliverables, acceptance, commercial owner, fee, duration, and next action.
- Added, changed, and absent-in-later-results comparison between retained editions.
- Immutable merchant preparation, original dataset preview, and adoption of an existing finalized buyer delivery.
- Exact CSV, source-edition, workshare brief, and portable workspace exports.

Set an explicit --receiving-root DIRECTORY when the browser should enumerate existing receiving folders outside the workspace. A retained source import is also available through the CLI below. Stop the server with Ctrl-C; committed source, reviews, and editions remain in the workspace.

## Save and acquire a real cohort

Create a query definition in a private JSON file:

~~~json
{
  "name": "Federal AI and IT prime awards — September to October 2026",
  "startDate": "2026-09-01",
  "endDate": "2026-10-11",
  "dateType": "new_awards_only",
  "keywords": ["artificial intelligence"],
  "naics": ["541511", "541512", "541513", "541519"],
  "awardTypes": ["A", "B", "C", "D"],
  "minimumAwardUsd": 100000,
  "maximumAwardUsd": 20000000,
  "pageSize": 50,
  "maxRows": 10000
}
~~~

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-research query-save \
  --workspace /private/federal-award-research --file /private/query.json

starforge usaspending-research capture \
  --workspace /private/federal-award-research --query RETURNED_QUERY_ID --revision 1
~~~

Additional filters are recipient, awardIds, psc, description, and agencies. Agencies are objects with type awarding or funding, tier toptier or subtier, and the exact agency name; subtier entries can include toptier_name. Date selection is explicit. The supported values are new_awards_only, action_date, date_signed, and last_modified_date. The provider's documented filter contract is linked in SOURCE_MAP.md.

Fresh acquisition uses the official USAspending search endpoint, the configured fields, and an Award ID ascending order. Each accepted source page retains its original request bytes and the entire original HTTP response. Provider continuation values become the next request; completion requires the provider's actual hasNext false. A retained imported capture keeps its original source fields and ordering, including an Award Amount descending query.

The workspace serializes requests, stores provider failures with their response bytes and retry time, and exposes a paused capture for operator resumption. It does not silently widen a query after a provider rejection. A complete cohort, a partial capture, an analyst selection, a standalone detail, and a received dataset view have separate coverage descriptions.

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-research resume \
  --workspace /private/federal-award-research --capture ORIGINAL_CAPTURE_ID
~~~

If the source cohort exceeds the selected local row capacity, the operator can explicitly increase it up to 250,000 using the original capture's current updated_at value:

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-research capacity \
  --workspace /private/federal-award-research --capture ORIGINAL_CAPTURE_ID \
  --max-rows 25000 --updated-at ORIGINAL_CURRENT_UPDATED_AT
~~~

The already accepted pages and the successful response that reached capacity stay attached to the original capture. A subsequent resume continues that capture.

# Award transactions and modifications

The transaction workspace extends the original USAspending award workspace. It follows federal funding actions, preserves every original source occurrence, compares later captures by transaction identity, and binds a private workshare assessment to the retained award and transaction observations.

Open **Transactions & modifications** in the workspace navigation, or **Research transaction history** from an individual award. The browser uses the existing private session, source client, SQLite database, job controller, and recovery flow.

## Operator workflow

1. Choose a retained award edition and its original generated award identity. Search the edition by prime, award, or description.
2. Capture its transaction history. Each accepted response is retained before the next page is requested. The progress panel shows original pages, returned rows, continuation, capacity, and any provider retry time.
3. Inspect chronological actions and federal fiscal-year subtotals. Open an action's original page and request receipt. Filter modification numbers, descriptions, action types, and dates.
4. Acquire a later observation when useful. Compare captures of the same award by transaction identity. Added, changed, absent, and conflicting identities retain coverage for both observations.
5. Save a private assessment describing fit, funding changes, proposed workshare, deliverables, acceptance, relationship owner, and next action.
6. Export the original source capture, spreadsheet CSV, or combined award and workshare brief. Receive the capture into a matching retained award edition. Full workspace backup includes all original pages and every review revision.

## Official source and financial interpretation

The acquisition endpoint follows the official [USAspending transaction contract](https://github.com/fedspendingtransparency/usaspending-api/blob/master/usaspending_api/api_contracts/contracts/v2/transactions.md):

    POST https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/transactions/

The request carries award_id, page, limit, sort, and order. Native acquisition uses action_date ascending; imported pages retain any supported official sort and order. Page size is 1–5,000, default 250. Local capacity is up to 250,000 returned source occurrences. A paused capture can increase its saved capacity. Completion follows contiguous original page metadata and the terminal hasNext:false.

Monetary values come from original JSON numeric tokens and use decimal strings and integer arithmetic. Null remains unknown. Every transaction retains its original identity, modification, date, classification, description, obligation, loan fields, source page, source position, and record hash.

Identical repeated records remain in the source export and count once in financial totals. Conflicting records for an identity remain available as original occurrences; affected totals are unknown and comparisons report the identity as unresolved. Conflicting dates spanning fiscal years appear in every affected year, with a possible action count when the year is ambiguous.

Positive obligation, deobligation, and zero change describe the amount independently of the agency's original action description. Award details and transaction histories have their own observation times; the displayed difference compares those retained observations. Federal fiscal years begin October 1. Same-day rows use transaction identity for deterministic presentation within the source's date precision.

## CLI

Use Node 22.13+ or 24. All commands use the existing CLI and private workspace. The following paths assume the seller SDK directory:

    node usaspending/cli.mjs serve --workspace /absolute/private/workspace --port 8783
    node usaspending/cli.mjs tx-state --workspace /absolute/private/workspace
    node usaspending/cli.mjs tx-capture --workspace /absolute/private/workspace \
      --edition EDITION_ID --key ORIGINAL_GENERATED_AWARD_ID --page-size 250 --max-rows 250000
    node usaspending/cli.mjs tx-resume --workspace /absolute/private/workspace --capture CAPTURE_ID
    node usaspending/cli.mjs tx-capacity --workspace /absolute/private/workspace \
      --capture CAPTURE_ID --max-rows 250000 --updated-at ORIGINAL_UPDATED_AT

Read and assess:

    node usaspending/cli.mjs tx-summary --workspace /absolute/private/workspace --capture CAPTURE_ID
    node usaspending/cli.mjs tx-browse --workspace /absolute/private/workspace \
      --capture CAPTURE_ID --search MODIFICATION --start-date 2026-01-01 --end-date 2026-12-31
    node usaspending/cli.mjs tx-compare --workspace /absolute/private/workspace \
      --before EARLIER_CAPTURE --after LATER_CAPTURE --out comparison.json
    node usaspending/cli.mjs tx-review --workspace /absolute/private/workspace \
      --capture CAPTURE_ID --revision 0 --file assessment.json

Assessment fields: status, fit, fundingChange, proposedWorkshare, deliverables, acceptance, owner, caseUrl, nextAction, notes. Status is researching, scope_match, review_with_owner, or passed. Scope match and owner review require fit, proposed workshare, deliverables, and acceptance. A save uses the current review revision to protect another operator's edits.

Export and receive:

    node usaspending/cli.mjs tx-source --workspace /absolute/private/workspace \
      --capture CAPTURE_ID --page 1 --out original-response.json
    node usaspending/cli.mjs tx-export --workspace /absolute/private/workspace \
      --capture CAPTURE_ID --out capture.json --include-reviews
    node usaspending/cli.mjs tx-csv --workspace /absolute/private/workspace \
      --capture CAPTURE_ID --out actions.csv --spreadsheet
    node usaspending/cli.mjs tx-brief --workspace /absolute/private/workspace \
      --capture CAPTURE_ID --out workshare.md
    node usaspending/cli.mjs tx-receive --workspace /absolute/private/receiving \
      --file capture.json --edition ORIGINAL_AWARD_EDITION --include-reviews

Output files are create-only. Source captures include a private assessment only when requested, and receiving that assessment is explicit. Received assessments retain original operator, time, revision, and prior receiving lineage. Repeated receiving preserves local edits and reports a conflict if a different assessment would replace them.

## Retained source imports

Import the original award detail or cohort first. The transaction import JSON has a pages array. Each page contains:

| Field | Required original value |
| --- | --- |
| request | Official request object: award_id, page, limit, sort, order |
| responseBase64 | Original response bytes, base64 encoded |
| receipt.status | Accepted HTTP status 200 |
| receipt.bytes | Original response byte count |
| receipt.sha256 | SHA-256 of the original response bytes |
| receipt.finishedAt | Original observation time |
| receipt.url | Official response URL, when retained |
| receipt.request.method | POST |
| receipt.request.url | Official transaction endpoint |
| receipt.request.body | Parsed original request object |
| receipt.request.bodyBase64 | Original request bytes |
| receipt.request.bodySha256 | SHA-256 of original request bytes |

Additional original metadata, including start time and headers, stays in the receipt. The import verifies request identity, exact bytes, page continuity, monetary projection, and original award binding before writes. Pages begin at 1; a partial contiguous prefix remains resumable.

    node usaspending/cli.mjs tx-import --workspace /absolute/private/workspace \
      --edition EDITION_ID --key ORIGINAL_GENERATED_AWARD_ID --file original-pages.json

## Persistence and recovery

The original awards.sqlite3 gains five additive transaction tables. Existing workspaces open directly, and older backups restore without transaction tables. New backups carry captures, pages, normalized occurrences, assessments, and review history.

Source acceptance and its normalized rows commit together. A successful response that exceeded local row capacity remains in the interrupted operation for replay after capacity is increased. Provider retry timing is honored. Pause and resume use the original workspace job controller.

Portable captures include the initial request, capacity, original pages, projected rows, coverage, and fingerprint. A prepared capture with zero accepted pages is portable and resumable. Workspace restore checks source bytes, request/response bindings, projected rows, contiguous positions, the full copied award row, continuation, completion, fingerprints, and assessment bindings before committing.

## Native receiving journey

Run the source-driven journey with an actual retained source packet and a new output directory:

    node usaspending/transactions/run-native.mjs --source ORIGINAL_SOURCE_PACKET.json \
      --out /absolute/private/transaction-receiving

The runner imports the original award and transaction source, opens the existing private HTTP operator, saves an internal source-bound assessment, writes exports and a brief, restores the full workspace, and receives the capture into the original award-only workspace. It compares the received rows with the actual original input. The output directory contains the working customer workspace and portable receiving package.

The cumulative Stellar Forge distribution includes these runtime modules and browser assets through its existing seller SDK component.

# Federal award workshare portfolio

Operate a set of retained awards through the original `AwardWorkspace` and
`AwardTransactions` APIs. The workbench adds capture selection, agency and
recipient rollups, private workshare editing, portable deliveries, and resumable
receiving. It does not create a second award database or contact prospects.

## Open the workbench

From `stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/usaspending`:

```sh
node transactions/portfolio-cli.mjs serve --workspace /path/to/private/workspace
```

Open the printed loopback URL in a browser. The fragment is a local session key;
keep that URL private. The interface is grayscale, searchable, keyboard usable,
and paginated at 50 awards per page. A history selector exposes alternative
captures. Review edits use the original revision-checked writer and retain the
award edition and source fingerprint. A concurrent edit returns the original
conflict instead of overwriting another operator's assessment.

## Select and export

```sh
node transactions/portfolio-cli.mjs export \
  --workspace /path/to/private/workspace \
  --out /path/to/new-delivery \
  --capture TC-FIRST --capture TC-SECOND --reviews
```

Omit `--capture` to select the newest complete capture for each award. An award
with no complete capture uses its newest partial capture. Every unselected
capture is recorded under `selection.alternatives`. Selecting two captures of
the same award fails instead of double-counting its obligations. A partial or
conflicted history remains visible and makes the complete-history total unknown.
Known captured amounts remain separately available. Decimal strings are summed
with integer arithmetic, including values above JavaScript's safe-integer range.
These are federal funding observations, not a forecast of the operator's revenue.

The delivery contains `portfolio.json`, `view.json`, spreadsheet-safe `awards.csv`,
`workshares.md`, each complete original capture under `captures/`, and a file
manifest. Each capture retains the original request/response bytes and original
export digest. The portfolio validates its summary against the normalized rows
when reopened. Export builds a private partial directory and publishes the
completed directory; the target must not already exist. A partial directory is
an interrupted build and can be removed after its contents are inspected.

Private assessments are excluded by default. `--reviews` or the browser's explicit
checkbox includes them. The workbench itself is a private operating surface and
shows existing reviews to its authenticated local operator.

## Receive and resume

First receive the original award edition in the destination's existing workspace.
Then use the original transaction receiver through the portfolio command:

```sh
node transactions/portfolio-cli.mjs receive \
  --workspace /path/to/receiving-workspace \
  --packet /path/to/delivery/portfolio.json \
  --journal /path/to/receiving-journal.json --reviews
```

The parent directory for the journal must exist. Reissue exactly the same command
after an interruption. The saved plan binds the portfolio digest, workspace ID,
review choice, and edition mapping. Each original capture is replayed through
`AwardTransactions.receive`, which owns source validation, award matching,
idempotent receiving and private-assessment conflict handling. Checkpoints are
written after each accepted capture. Replaying checkpoints also repairs a target
workspace restored from an earlier backup. A failed capture is recorded with its
original error; prior accepted captures stay available.

When original editions have different IDs in the destination, `--edition-map`
accepts a JSON file mapping original edition IDs to receiving edition IDs. The
original receiver still requires the award row digest to match. Changing the
source, destination or review plan requires a different journal file. Use one
receiving process per journal; separate workers should use separate journals.

## Inspect without opening a workspace

```sh
node transactions/portfolio-cli.mjs inspect --packet delivery/portfolio.json
```

This works on Node 22 without package installation. Operating an original SQLite
workspace requires the product's Node 22.13+ runtime. No dependencies, provider
calls, scheduled jobs or GitHub Actions workflows are added.

## Acceptance

```sh
node transactions/portfolio-acceptance.mjs
```

The component journey uses a deterministic fixture implementing the public
transaction-store interface. It covers 10,000 awards, exact decimals, duplicate
award selection, archive contents, digest/summary binding, interrupted receiving,
replay, workspace-plan binding, loopback HTTP, stale review revisions and private
export opt-in. It is distinct from the full original USAspending source → merchant
→ Applications receiving journey. The CLI and server load the original
`../workspace.mjs` for actual workspaces.
